question: Which conversion laws share an owner across formats, and what Markdown reuse contract preserves every partial-prefix result without repeated whole-response work?
trigger: User requested a final first-principles review of the latest imports, exports, HTML, Markdown and streaming work and a ranked next step.
requirements: Reconcile current implementation and later proof with prior reviews before reopening decisions.
Every read used by a projected preview, static HTML export or copy must observe the same immutable document without mutating the source editor.
Reuse unchanged rendering only when local and cross-document dependencies permit it; preserve concurrent and server rendering.
Explicit conversion diagnostics must report omitted content properties; an encoder existing is not evidence that it emitted a property.
Retain adopted dialect semantics, schema authority, safety, consumer-owned accept/cancel/undo and opt-in paste UI unless contradictory evidence warrants reopening.
Review and record only; do not edit product code or the active implementation plan.
evidenceReuse: Reconciled the conversion-boundary review and all five subsequent bound execution records, latest conversion/format-mapping decisions, current static-preview plan, live parser/consumer/static-renderer source, and the existing six-repository prior-art study. Reused historical package/browser proof only for its recorded sources and scope. Ran two new current-source public-boundary probes and consumed one bounded independent HTML review. This is a next-work assessment of five selected domains, not an exhaustive function or mapping audit.
summary: Pursue immutable document-read coherence and dependency-correct static rendering first. The document prop is the right small caller shape, but createProjectedEditorView overrides read while inherited plugin portals remain bound to the source view: both EditorStatic and renderStaticHtml produce a SOURCE TOC beside a PROJECTED body. Replace that partial facade at the existing Plite view/runtime owner, adapted by Plate, before optimizing reuse. HTML fidelity accounting ranks second: image title is omitted with no diagnostic because compiled encoder ownership grants blanket property coverage. Retain adopted document conversion, Markdown grammar/mappings/previous-result reuse, shared safety and app-owned paste feedback. No universal codec, parser-engine replacement, public view hook or mutable stable view is justified. Five of eight new projection benchmark cells pass; three are inconclusive, and source changes require bounded reruns.

alternatives: Keep current APIs and configure registry callers: reject for projected reads because a legitimate component reading through its supplied editor gets source-derived plugin data. More caller glue preserves the defect.

Keep document as the public input and change the existing view/read owner: pursue. Bind all document-dependent operations to one immutable snapshot, then let static rendering use explicit dependency-correct reuse.
Add a public useEditorDocumentView or stream-session object: reject absent an independent job; the document prop and existing previous-result contract already express the consumer inputs.

Delete the partial spread-and-override editor facade: strongest cut. Compare a correctly rebound existing read-only runtime with a smaller snapshot reader; do not choose a new public type before the ownership proof.
Use a stable mutable view or memoize by element identity alone: reject without concurrency and cross-document dependency laws; TOC, roots, lists and decorations can change outside a node.
Rebuild conversion around a universal codec/AST or replace micromark: reject for this next step; the concrete failures are read binding and fidelity accounting, not syntax representation.
Patch only image title: insufficient. Add preservation or a diagnostic for that case, but the lasting HTML repair is actual emission accounting at the compiler rather than blanket owner coverage.
proofLimits: New headless Bun/React probes reproduce projected direct-read versus plugin-read divergence through EditorStatic and renderStaticHtml, and silent image title loss through semantic HTML serialize/server parse. Both intentionally exit 1 while the defect remains and record exact source hashes. No browser, clipboard, RSC concurrency, full package suite or benchmark was rerun in this review. Existing projection matrix has 5 pass/3 inconclusive cells (2 baseline warmup timeouts, 1 variation failure); relevant source hashes have since shifted, so it cannot certify the current path. Prior conversion acceptance is retained only within its original scope. Detailed static dependency architecture and the full HTML emission census remain design/proof work. Repository inventory may drift while the separate static-preview plan is in progress; refresh never upgrades historical proof.
